newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies approve telecommunications bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies approve telecommunications bill.

text.p: Brazil's lower house of Congress approved a bill that regulates telecommunications sector and lays down rules for the privatization of the federal Telebras system, an official said.

The Chamber of Deputies voted 312-99 in favor of the bill. Three lawmakers abstained. A series of amendments were also due to be voted on in the Chamber of Deputies before the legislation advances to the Senate.

Among the amendments is a proposal that would strike down one of the bill's most important articles by preventing private telecommunications companies from setting their own rates three years after beginning operations.
Other amendments would set limits on foreign capital involved in telecommunications operators and change rules included in the bill for a new sector regulator.
The government needs a straight majority of the deputies present in the chamber to defeat each amemdment.

The bill regulates a constitutional reform approved by Congress in 1995 which did away with the state's monopoly in telecommunications. The government hopes to begin privatizing Telebras by the end of the year.
